purpose: Authorize exactly the write surface needed for a thin, bounded, stdlib-only Campaign Supervisor that schedules one-round-at-a-time wake-ups of the already-PASS GPT<->Hermes bridge for a single milestone. This package authorizes the Supervisor contract; it implements nothing itself.

architecture.gpt: GPT-5.6 (the external driver that emits control envelopes and decides milestone outcomes)
architecture.supervisor: orchestration/hermes/supervisor/ — the new thin wake-up / scheduling layer this contract authorizes
architecture.bridge: orchestration/hermes/bridge/ — the existing one-round GPT<->Hermes control kernel; READ-ONLY here and the sole task-authorization authority
architecture.hermes: Hermes / DeepSeek (the execution side the bridge already drives)
architecture.flow: GPT-5.6 <-> Campaign Supervisor <-> existing bridge_cli.py ONE ROUND <-> Hermes / DeepSeek

interfaces: bridge_cli.py round — invoke exactly ONE bridge round
bridge_state.load_state() / BridgeState.as_dict() — read the chain state (expected_sequence, expected_nonce, expected_in_reply_to, status, last_result_sha256)
bridge_state.read_pending() — resolve a durable pending result at startup
bridge_state.bridge_lock — the Bridge's own single-worker guard
chatgpt_adapter.read_latest_assistant() — the deterministic READ seam for the latest completed assistant response and its sha256
read_only_reuse.note: The Supervisor wraps these interfaces. It does not copy, edit or vendor them, and it introduces no duplicate task-authorization layer.

may_do: poll the latest completed assistant response and compute its sha256
never process the same assistant response twice
invoke bridge_cli.py round exactly once per valid new expected task
wait for the next new assistant response
validate and honour a campaign-terminal envelope
persist bounded campaign state and exit
must_not_do: redesign, replace or copy the Bridge
auto-repair a Bridge safety state or edit Bridge state

campaign_protocol.note: The marker constants are composed at runtime from their components in code; the literal delimiter is deliberately not written in this package's prose.
campaign_protocol.terminal_effect: persist terminal state, journal it, exit; never call bridge_cli.py round, so the Bridge stays WAITING_FOR_GPT with its next sequence available for the next milestone

state_model.durability: atomic replace plus fsync where practical
state_model.primary_guard: the latest completed assistant response sha256; the Bridge's sequence / nonce / replay remains authoritative
state_model.single_owner: only one Supervisor process may own a campaign

bridge_states.note: No auto-repair, no manual Bridge state edit. A durable pending result on startup is reconciled by invoking bridge_cli.py round exactly once for the Bridge's own startup reconciliation.

gpt_decides: failed item repairable -> next valid Bridge task
human approval required -> campaign terminal HUMAN_REQUIRED
task_outcome_policy.note: A Bridge result of FAILED/BLOCKED does not itself cause an automatic retry; the Supervisor waits for the next new assistant response unless the Bridge entered a safety state.

bounded_autonomy.on_limit: persist PAUSED with outcome LIMIT_REACHED and exit; no infinite autonomy

read_first.why: the one-round entry point the Supervisor invokes exactly once per new valid task; read-only
the HERMES_TASK_V1 / HERMES_RESULT_V1 envelope, strict JSON decoding and field validation the Supervisor reuses read-only
chain state, replay journal, durable pending result and the single-worker lock the Supervisor reads read-only
the deterministic READ seam for the latest completed assistant response and its sha256 the Supervisor wraps
the contract gate and guarded execution path that remain entirely inside the Bridge
the orchestration layer's own entry description and boundaries
how the orchestration layer integrates, confirming the Supervisor consumes existing seams only

boundary_notes.resolution: allowed_paths and forbidden_paths are project-relative to the Contract Guard source_root; an entry is a directory prefix or an exact file.
boundary_notes.two_allowed_directories: Exactly two directories are allowed: the Supervisor package and its evidence directory. No parent directory above either is allow-listed, so the authorization cannot widen into the Bridge or the control plane.
boundary_notes.no_overlap: No allowed path is equal to, inside, or a parent of any forbidden path; the compiler reports zero E_PATH_CONFLICT.
boundary_notes.unlisted_is_blocked: Any path inside the project root matching neither list stays BLOCKED (UNCLASSIFIED_FAIL_CLOSED), which protects the Bridge, the compiler, the guard and every historical artifact.
boundary_notes.bridge_immutable: orchestration/hermes/bridge/ is forbidden for writes and is proven byte-identical by pre/post sha256 comparison.

contract_notes.generated_artifacts_owner: the deterministic Specification Compiler only; never hand-patched
contract_notes.this_session: CONTRACT_AUTHORING_ONLY — authors and validates the contract package; implements nothing
contract_notes.implementation_next: a later human-approved installation session implements the Supervisor inside the authorized write surface
